subject: A slogan on the wall, ink on the finger
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: on a grey wall, in huge letters of blue ink, is written: 'MODI KAHIN NAHI JAYEGA', meaning 'Modi is not going anywhere'. The ink runs down from the letters and drips to the floor. In front of the wall a figure with a white beard, glasses and a saffron jacket kneels and paints the slogan with a brush, holding a jar marked 'INK'; blue ink streams over his head, face and clothes. On the right a young man in a blue shirt raises his finger, which bears the mark of voting ink, and says: 'SIR, THIS INK WILL DECIDE!' The cartoonist's signature in the corner: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: On one side, so much ink is being poured on the wall that the slogan itself has run down and spread over the floor, and the man writing it is soaked in it from head to toe: Modi is not going anywhere. On the other side, a young man simply raises one finger, carrying a small mark of ink.

Satish Acharya's jab is at this difference. However large the writing on the walls, who stays and who goes is decided by the ink put on a voter's finger on polling day. The slogan is loud, but the last word belongs to that small mark, provided every citizen still has the right to cast a vote.
